workflow_steps.objective: Confirm the product benefit, retail audience, brand inputs, physical constraints, retailer requirements, success criteria, approvals, and unresolved information.
Assess category conventions, competing pet-care tools, consumer comprehension barriers, shelf context, and relevant retailer and manufacturing constraints.
Set decision criteria for immediate benefit comprehension, product visibility, protection, brand recognition, accessibility, sustainability, and retail impact.
Define the packaging format, exact product fit, retention and protection method, display orientation, information hierarchy, required panels, and retail features.
Create and test rough structural prototypes for fit, protection, assembly, product removal, shelf presentation, and legibility at retail distance.
Develop meaningfully different structural and graphic packaging directions that demonstrate the unfamiliar tool and communicate its benefit.
Compare concepts against the agreed criteria and obtain explicit client approval of one direction.
Incorporate feedback into the selected concept, resolving structure, instructional communication, claims, hierarchy, graphics, and finishes.
Create accurate cutting, folding, bleed, safe-area, glue, fastening, and product-retention geometry for the approved structure.
Prepare preflighted print-ready artwork and manufacturing specifications using confirmed printer, substrate, finish, color, barcode, and retailer requirements.
Validate and hand off approved production masters, dielines, specifications, mockups, and prototype documentation.

missing_inputs: Physical product sample or verified CAD, dimensions, tolerances, weight, center of gravity, materials, moving parts, and fragile surfaces
Required protection level, distribution conditions, tamper resistance, security, product access, and package-life expectations
Approved brand identity files, usage guidelines, mandatory marks, tone, and existing packaging conventions
Validated product benefit, usage sequence, approved claims, warnings, legal copy, translations, and regulatory requirements
Target consumers, retail price position, sales channels, shelf or peg context, competitive set, and comprehension success criteria
Major-retailer packaging, merchandising, barcode, labeling, accessibility, sustainability, testing, and vendor-compliance requirements
Printer or converter capabilities, preferred structure, substrate, minimum tolerances, finishes, color standard, supplied dieline requirements, and proofing process
Forecast quantity, budget, schedule, sustainability goals, approval owners, and required review milestones
assumptions: The scope covers one launch SKU rather than a differentiated packaging family.
A usable brand identity will be supplied; creating or redesigning the identity is outside the current packaging scope.
The unfamiliar product will require concise on-pack explanation supported by diagrams, product visibility, or both, subject to concept testing.
The final structure and production files will be based on verified physical-product data and printer or converter specifications, not estimated dimensions.
All product claims, warnings, retailer requirements, barcodes, and legal content will receive client or specialist approval before release.
stop_conditions: Do not finalize the structural specification or prototype without a verified product sample or dimensional data and defined protection requirements.
Do not select or refine a concept until the client explicitly approves one direction against agreed evaluation criteria.
Do not finalize the dieline until prototype testing confirms fit, retention, assembly, access, protection, and retail presentation.
Do not prepare production masters until approved copy, claims, warnings, brand assets, barcode data, retailer requirements, and printer or converter specifications are available.
Do not release files for manufacture until the client, retailer where required, and production vendor approve the final structure, proofs, materials, finishes, and preflight results.
rationale: This is a single-product concept-to-production packaging brief: it begins with comprehension and retail research, resolves physical structure through specification and prototyping, includes explicit client concept selection, and concludes with validated dieline and print-ready production deliverables.
